question: At what Projection payload class does the m12 transport/error behavior appear, and is that behavior sufficient to reproduce failure to recognize the context call as completed?

predecessors.m13: All four compact 4bit/8bit by low/high cells recognized one completed context call.

ordered_variants.content: metadata, target, and declared information loss
frozen projection without sources or extraction diagnostics
complete frozen projection plus benchmark receipts

receipt_design.purpose: Separate call recognition, front-of-result availability, end-of-result loss, truncation markers, and error transport.

adaptive_phase_2.condition: Run only if phase 1 contains both recognized and not-recognized outcomes.
adaptive_phase_2.cells: largest recognized payload and smallest not-recognized payload
adaptive_phase_2.order: ascending payload size, alternating cells by replicate
adaptive_phase_2.purpose: Check whether the observed boundary is stable enough to attribute to payload class rather than a single stochastic run.

deterministic_measures: tool-result is_error field and Exit code prefix
presence of header nonce, trailer nonce, and truncation marker
context call count and complete tool sequence
exact receipt fields written to probe.json
success: Exactly Bash then Write, one context call, available receipt values copied exactly, visible truncation/error classified exactly, and completed/no-repeat booleans true/false.
interpretation_ceiling: The experiment can isolate payload-class-associated Claude tool transport and immediate call recognition. It does not test full review convergence, cannot observe applied server reasoning effort, and one phase-1 replicate alone cannot establish a stochastic rate.
